title: SuperCLUE November 2026: Category Leaders and the Full 19-Model Score Ranking
gist: SuperCLUE's Nov 5, 2026 Chinese benchmark (19 models) has closed Gemini-4-Argon (73.62) and GPT-6.1-Sol (71.76) on top, with open Kimi-K3.1-Pro (61.46) third and leading open models in three of five categories, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash leading open coding and VIDRAFT's Darwin-180B-RSI-R3 leading open math/science reasoning. The community post is written by VIDRAFT_LAB, Darwin's developer, so its framing highlights Darwin; its main analytical point is that category-level scores diverge sharply from aggregate rank.

themes.theme: Closed frontier lead over open models

insights.claim: In SuperCLUE's November 2026 results, closed models Gemini-4-Argon (73.62) and GPT-6.1-Sol (71.76) top the overall score table, roughly 10-12 points above the best open model, Kimi-K3.1-Pro (61.46).
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Google and OpenAI retain a material frontier lead over open-weight (largely Chinese) models, supporting closed-model pricing power.
insights.locator: All 19 models in descending overall score order

insights.claim: Gemini-4-Argon leads SuperCLUE hallucination control (83.19) and ultra-long context (95.63), while GPT-6.1-Sol leads agentic coding (69.23) and mathematical and scientific reasoning (76.32); the two tie at 68.97 in precise instruction following.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Google and OpenAI have differentiated strengths (reliability/long context vs coding/reasoning), suggesting segmented rather than winner-take-all enterprise adoption.

insights.claim: The largest gap between the overall leader and the best open model on SuperCLUE is in precise instruction following, where Gemini/GPT score 68.97 versus Kimi-K3.1-Pro's 44.83, a 24.14-point gap.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Instruction following (key for agentic automation and structured outputs) is where open models lag most, a moat for closed API providers in enterprise automation.

insights.claim: Gemini-4-Argon leads Kimi-K3.1-Pro by 15.41 points in SuperCLUE hallucination control, though Kimi scores 4.17 points above GPT-6.1-Sol in that category.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Google's lead on factual reliability is a selling point for regulated/document-QA workloads.

insights.claim: Kimi-K3.1-Pro is the highest-scoring open model on SuperCLUE November 2026 (61.46 overall), leading open models in hallucination control, instruction following and ultra-long context, and ranking No. 1 in SuperCLUE's numbered ranking.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Moonshot's Kimi line has the strongest all-round open-model position among Chinese labs, relevant for China AI competitive dynamics.

insights.claim: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is the open-model leader in SuperCLUE agentic coding at 65.38, matching closed Gemini-4-Argon and trailing GPT-6.1-Sol by 3.85 points, and 7.69 points ahead of Kimi-K3.1-Pro.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: An open 'Flash' model matching a frontier closed model on agentic coding pressures pricing for coding-assistant APIs.

insights.claim: In ultra-long context on SuperCLUE, open Kimi-K3.1-Pro (87.25) trails closed GPT-6.1-Sol (88.14) by only 0.89 points, while DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 scores just 66.25.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Long-context capability is near-commoditized at the GPT level among open models, eroding a premium feature.

insights.claim: SuperCLUE's published table of 19 models contains 12 labeled open and seven labeled closed, and its numbered rank excludes international models (Gemini, GPT, Grok, Darwin) as a ranking-policy convention rather than a performance judgment.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Headline 'No. 1' claims from Chinese labs citing SuperCLUE rank exclude Western models; read raw scores, not policy ranks.
insights.quote: International models and some domestic models are excluded from ranking and shown for reference only.

insights.claim: SuperCLUE's open/closed labels are not an independent assessment of license terms, training-data disclosure, code availability, or commercial-use eligibility, so deployment decisions need separate license checks.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: 'Open' in leaderboards does not equal commercially usable; licensing risk remains for enterprises adopting Chinese open models.

insights.claim: Chinese mid-tier models cluster tightly on SuperCLUE overall score: Doubao-Seed-2.1-Pro-260915 (42.06), MiniMax M3.1-Flash (41.35), Step-5-Preview (41.23) and MiniMax-M3 (41.17) all share numbered rank 6, with Qwen3.8-Max-0902 at 43.22 and Hy4-Preview at 42.96 sharing rank 5.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Below Kimi/DeepSeek/GLM, Chinese labs (ByteDance, MiniMax, StepFun, Alibaba, Tencent) are effectively undifferentiated on capability, implying competition on price and distribution.

insights.claim: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max-0902 is labeled closed by SuperCLUE and scores only 43.22 overall, placing eighth of 19 and behind open GLM-5.3 (50.66) and GLM-5.3-Flash (47.18).
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Qwen's flagship trailing Zhipu's GLM open models on a Chinese benchmark is a notable competitive signal within China's model market.
insights.locator: All 19 models in descending overall score order

insights.claim: A model's position in an aggregate benchmark need not match its position on the task a developer needs, as shown by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 beating higher-overall Kimi-K3.1-Pro in coding.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Multi-model routing by task is more rational than single-vendor selection, benefiting model routers and evaluation tooling.
insights.quote: a model’s position in an aggregate benchmark need not match its position on the task a developer actually needs

insights.claim: Spark-X2.6 scores 68.42 in SuperCLUE reasoning but only 26.92 in coding and 12.07 in precise instruction following, showing that strength on one evaluation does not carry over automatically.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Spiky capability profiles mean single-number benchmarks can badly mislead procurement decisions.
insights.quote: Strong performance on one evaluation does not carry over automatically to the others.

insights.claim: GLM-5.3 scores 53.85 in coding and 77.60 in ultra-long context but only 17.24 in precise instruction following, and its smaller sibling GLM-5.3-Flash beats it on hallucination control (48.89 vs 43.61).
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Model naming and tier are unreliable guides to task performance; cheaper variants can outperform flagships on specific axes.
insights.quote: Model naming and aggregate placement are therefore insufficient guides to performance on this category.

insights.claim: SuperCLUE hallucination-control scores are not hallucination rates: a score of 83.19 cannot be converted into an 83.19% hallucination rate or a 16.81% error rate without the task definitions and scoring protocol.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Vendor marketing that translates benchmark points into reliability percentages should be discounted.
insights.quote: These scores are not hallucination rates.

insights.claim: SuperCLUE's detailed task definitions, confidence intervals and aggregate weighting formula were not verified, so the overall score should not be reconstructed as a simple average of the five categories.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Benchmark opacity limits how much weight investors should put on small leaderboard differences.
insights.quote: The published scores are benchmark results, not statistical guarantees.

insights.claim: A long-context benchmark score does not specify a model's maximum context window, and accepting a large input is distinct from reliably retrieving information from its middle or connecting evidence across documents.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Advertised context-window size is a weak proxy for real long-document capability.

insights.claim: For deployment, models should be validated on the intended language and tasks under consistent prompts, inference budgets and tool access, recording model revision, inference engine, precision and hardware, and measuring latency, memory and cost alongside correctness; Chinese-focused benchmark results should be retested for Korean or other languages.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Enterprise model selection increasingly requires in-house evaluation infrastructure, a demand driver for eval tooling vendors.
insights.locator: Applying the results to real workloads

themes.theme: Korea's Darwin as an open reasoning contender

insights.claim: VIDRAFT's Darwin-180B-RSI-R3, the only model from a Korean developer among the 19 SuperCLUE entries, scores 73.68 in mathematical and scientific reasoning, second overall behind GPT-6.1-Sol (76.32) and first among open models, while placing only ninth overall at 43.08.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: A Korean open model with a narrow reasoning strength signals sovereign-AI efforts outside the US/China duopoly, though the article is self-authored by the developer.
insights.quote: a Korean-developed open model stands near the top of this evaluation in mathematical and scientific reasoning

insights.claim: Darwin-180B-RSI-R3 outscores closed Gemini-4-Argon and Grok-4.7 in SuperCLUE mathematical and scientific reasoning (73.68 vs 71.05 and 68.42).
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Specialized open models can beat frontier closed models on narrow domains, supporting vertical/specialist model strategies.
